messages:
sasha: Heads-up — noticed a spike of reconnects for /v1/stream (EU) right after the canary rolled yesterday 22:10 UTC. Console shows a flurry of session_closed events but quotas and token usage look steady. cc @akhil @maria :thinking_face:
akhil: Which protocol? SSE or WS? any sample headers / proxy in front of it?
sasha: SSE. Proxy config changed to lower idle window in canary (from 90s -> 30s). Repro locally with: curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-test' — server sends keepalives but client sees `204` then reconnect.
ingress-bot: Alert: stream.session_close_rate on route /v1/stream eu-west-1 exceeded 3x baseline (22:07–22:18 UTC). Alert ID A-28733.
maria: I pulled console logs. Sampling suggests cluster-side keepalive window is preemptively closing sockets (204 path) while runtime emits a client_close shortly after. The console aggregates session_close_reason into a single bucket, so 204 != client_disconnect in charts and the UI hides that as "normal". Looks like the new proxy idle window induces a hysteresis where proxy emits 204 -> client reconnect -> runtime counts a new session (billing risk).
sasha: That would explain duplicate session events and the billing noise we saw. We also saw routing fallback to dedicated-cheaper region for some requests during the canary — potential double-sending?
ben: We should avoid cross-region fallback during canary. Propose sticky-routing for in-flight SSE: route by session_id -> same shard. Quick patch I tested: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  streamSticky: "true"
  streamIdleMs: "60000"
```
kubectl apply -f patch-sticky.yaml
This prevents the resume+fallback handshake from hitting multiple backends.
akhil: Also we'll need telemetry tags to disambiguate close reasons at ingest. I can add a metric `stream.proxy_keepalive_ms` and tag `route_version` so console can split counts by proxy version. Cost-wise this is low cardinality and okay.
maria: Agree. Also adding an annotation in the rollout UI that surfaces per-route keepalive/idle settings would help on-call. Right now SREs have to jump between infra configs and console graphs.
sasha: Product/ops ask — impact numbers? rough baseline for last 12h?
nina: pinging for customer impact summary. Ops needs delta to decide whether to rollback canary.
sasha: Quick numbers: ~2.1k sessions affected in eu-west over 11m window, ~6% reconnect rate spike, estimated extra 0.8% token billing churn. Most users unaffected but tail clients with long-polling hit it.
maria: I rolled a hotfix to the canary pool: increased proxy idle window to 75s for canary nodes and enabled sticky-routing for /v1/stream. Will monitor.
deploy-bot: deploy success: canary/proxy-config v1.12.4 -> 176515 in eu-west (2026-03-22T22:34:10Z) :rocket:
sasha: Thanks — I'll keep an eye on the console and follow up with a playbook entry. Can we get the telemetry change + console annotation in the next patch so we don't have to guess next time?
akhil: Yep I'll open a PR with the metric and add a lightweight ingest tag.
ben: I'll send the sticky config as a feature-flagged rollout so we can enable per-route.
maria: Filed follow-ups: infra#3245 (telemetry), infra#3246 (console annotation), ops#789 (playbook).
sasha: Great. tagging everyone here for monitoring: @maria @akhil @ben @nina. Will close thread if metrics stabilize by 23:00 UTC.
